headline: Heard an appeal over which side of a fence at 485 South Union Street counts as finished for permit closure.
summary: Alexander Garlick appealed an administrative decision on permit ZPF-24-63 for a fence at 485 South Union Street. Staff said the fence style changed, which required a permit, and that the unfinished side faces the neighboring properties. Garlick said the placement of the posts, not the finished side, sets the fence's direction, and the hearing closed so the board could deliberate.

## MINUTES

*Hybrid & In Person (at 645 Pine Street) Meeting*

**Board Members Present:** Caitlin Halpert, Evan Gould, Geoff Hand, Sean McKenzie, Miles Waite, Chase Taylor, and Marina Loughlin

   1. **ZAP-26-14; 485 South Union Street (RM, Ward 6) Elise Tarbi / Alexander Garlick**
   Appeal of administrative decision of ZPF-24-63 for which side of the fence is finished for permit closure. (Project Manager, Matthew Clark)
   Elise Tarbi, owner, present, Alexander Garlick: Sworn in.

   Evan Gould: This is an appeal of an administrative decision. Is the appellant present?

   Alexander Garlick: Yes.

   Evan Gould: In the case of appeals, we will hear the facts of the case from City staff, then open it up for the appellant to speak. Can you tell us about the facts of this case and decision?

   Matthew Clark: This is in regards to ZPF-24-63. As it stands, the first permit condition presents language of the orientation on the finished side of the fence. The unfinished side of the fence is facing outward towards the abutting properties. This is not a repair of an existing fence, but the installation of a new style of fence. The photos of what previously existed do not match what was installed.

   Sean McKenzie: Where are the pictures taken from?

   Alexander Garlick: The opposite site of the property line facing outwards.

   Geoff Hand: The old fence appears to be a picket style fence, while the new installation appears to be a stockade fence.

   Caitlin Halpert: I have a question on whether this fence is in kind or not. From the project plans, it appears the completed fence matches what was included with the approved project plans.

   Matthew Clark: Correct, but from my interpretation of this because the style of fence has changed this is what required a permit.

   Geoff Hand: But if they have a permit for the work the appeal is based off of which orientation the finished side is facing. The type of fencing installed matches the approved plans, it just was not installed right.

   Evan Gould: Are there any additional questions or comments from members of the Board? Hearing none, we will now open it up to the appellant to speak.

   Alexander Garlick: I think you are all caught up to the details on the facts of the case. The submitted photographs are from when we first purchased the property in 2022. It was overgrown for a portion of time and was blown over by the wind. We eventually found a contractor willing to work in Burlington who completed the work in fall 2024. I consulted with my neighbors about a replacement fence. I am not disputing the finished versus unfinished side, but the location of the posts that determine which way the fence is facing. It was a communication with the Zoning Division that led to this issue. Unfortunately, the contractor finished the project, so I have no way to undo what was already completed. That is my narrative and I raised a technical point in my appeal. Afterwards, the Zoning Division informed me

   Evan Gould: The previous fence was a stockade fence.

   Alexander Garlick: What is a stockade fence?

   Miles Waite: A fence composed of vertical slats, tightly grouped.

   Caitlin Halpert: A zoning permit was required for the visual change in fence type.

   Alexander Garlick: I did not know emailing through the online OpenGov permitting portal, but a privacy fence is described as something that cannot be seen through.

   Evan Gould: Are there any additional questions or comments from the Board?

   Sean McKenzie: Do you know the difference between a stockade fence and a picket fence?

   Alexander Garlick: Yes.

   Evan Gould: Are there any questions or comments from members of the public attending in person or online? Hearing none, we will close the hearing on this item to deliberate on it.

5. **Adjournment**

   Hearing closed at 5:35 PM.
